datasets.name: Fruit Lab
datasets.description: Learn with familiar apples, oranges and bananas. These classroom examples are prepared for this activity.

columns.name: size
columns.label: Size
columns.description: How big the fruit is, on a scale from 1 to 10.

columns.name: sweetness
columns.label: Sweetness
columns.description: How sweet the fruit is, on a scale from 1 to 10.

datasets.licence: Original classroom examples created for this project.
datasets.preprocessing: Hand-authored teaching examples. Numeric scores are illustrative, not scientific measurements. Classification uses numeric size, sweetness and weight; clustering uses only selected numeric features.

datasets.name: Iris Flower Lab
datasets.description: Explore measurements from 150 real iris flowers collected for scientific study.

columns.name: sepal_length_cm
columns.label: Sepal length
columns.description: Length of the outer, leaf-like part of the flower.

columns.name: sepal_width_cm
columns.label: Sepal width
columns.description: Width of the outer, leaf-like part of the flower.

columns.name: species
columns.label: Fruit name
columns.description: The flower type recorded by researchers. This is the answer for classification, never a clustering input.

datasets.licence: CC BY 4.0 (verify current repository terms before redistribution outside this project).
datasets.attribution: Iris dataset, UCI Machine Learning Repository. DOI: 10.24432/C56C76. Original data associated with R. A. Fisher (1936).
datasets.preprocessing: CSV prepared from the classic 150-row Iris dataset. Measurements retain the original centimetre values and one decimal place; no rows were filtered. Column names were made web-friendly.
